entries.review_description: Drawing canvas. The blank drawing surface and its resting canvas chrome. Captured in light mode on iPhone 13 mini in portrait at 375 × 812. Assess visible hierarchy, spacing, text fit, clipping, overlap, touch-target clarity, modal scrolling, and visual consistency. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: The blank drawing surface and its resting canvas chrome.
entries.critique: The bottom-left chevron is faint enough against the pale canvas that it is easy to miss at a glance; the settings icon remains more legible.
entries.recommendation: Increase the chevron’s contrast slightly while keeping it visually quieter than the drawing tools.

Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.

Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.

Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.

entries.review_description: Grown-Ups Only gate. The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation. Captured in night mode on iPhone 13 mini in portrait at 375 × 812. Assess only night-mode contrast and legibility. Ignore layout and responsive composition. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.

entries.review_description: Admin · access-code actions. The modal action sheet on phones and inline actions on tablets. Captured in light mode on iPhone 13 mini in portrait at 375 × 812. Assess visible hierarchy, spacing, text fit, clipping, overlap, touch-target clarity, modal scrolling, and visual consistency. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.

Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.

Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.

entries.review_description: Android beta. Google Play closed-test sign-up instructions. Captured in night mode on iPhone 16 Pro Max in landscape at 956 × 440. Assess only night-mode contrast and legibility. Ignore layout and responsive composition. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. entries.review_description: Coloring page · applied. A selected page with its active-page chip. Captured in light mode on iPhone 16 Pro Max in landscape at 956 × 440. Assess visible hierarchy, spacing, text fit, clipping, overlap, touch-target clarity, modal scrolling, and visual consistency. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. entries.review_description: Stroke-width menu. Line-width choices with live brush previews. Captured in night mode on iPad Pro 13-inch (M4) in landscape at 1376 × 1032. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the screen corner, are deliberately styled quieter than the drawing tools so they recede next to the child’s artwork. They are still meant to be plainly visible, so report them if they are genuinely hard to make out against what is behind them. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is the intended affordance rather than a rendering artifact. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation.
